payload:
[CORRECTION to my own signal cowork-team-20260824T203850Z, committed 6ea6b30f9, already drained to processed/] I OVERSTATED THE SCOPE. That signal called the CCATO gate's verdicts 'WRONG BY CONSTRUCTION' and 'structurally wrong'. Measured across the full cohort 12 minutes later, the defect affects EXACTLY 1 OF 110 ROWS. Read this before actioning the earlier signal.

WHAT FALSIFIED IT: a second CCATO row from the same gate, same cycle, 3 minutes after my exhibit -- `ntg-20260824T203614Z-technical_indicators-VNM-82a3ee`, from=po. claim: 'VNM chua co du lieu chi bao ky thuat' (VNM has no technical indicator data). tool: get_technical_indicators. ticker VNM == probe_ticker VNM. returned_value carries real values: NEUTRAL, RSI 64.196, MACD {value 1298.87, signal 1124.21, histogram 174.66}, Bollinger {upper 64434.06, middle 61430, lower 58425.94}. The probe carries exactly the field the claim is about, the subject matches, and the data is genuinely present. THAT VERDICT IS CORRECT -- a true positive. The gate works on this path.

FULL-COHORT PARTITION (110 ntg-* rows in signal_queue, measured 20:47Z):
  tool=get_technical_indicators : 109  (ticker == probe_ticker in all 109)
  tool=get_macro_snapshot       :   1  (ticker='macro' vs probe_ticker='VIRA' -- MISMATCHED)
  ticker == probe_ticker        : 109/110
  the single mismatch IS my exhibit (ntg-20260824T203331Z, from=tran-ngoc-bau)

CORRECTED FINDING: it is not the gate that is structurally wrong -- it is the `get_macro_snapshot` PROBE PATH specifically. That path is exercised by exactly one row in the entire cohort, is the only ticker/probe_ticker mismatch, and produced a false contradiction against a TRUE claim (CPI and VIRA genuinely absent from the macro snapshot payload). Reads as an undertested branch: the technical_indicators path is exercised 109x and behaves correctly on the instance I could verify; the macro path fired once and was wrong.

WHAT STANDS FROM THE EARLIER SIGNAL, UNCHANGED:
- The exhibit itself is valid. The macro/VIRA row IS a false positive with the mechanism described (probe response contains no CPI and no VIRA field, so 'non-null' cannot falsify the claim).
- The acceptance test is still the right fix and is still worth adding: an absence-claim naming field X must be probed with a tool whose response schema CONTAINS X; if none exists, ABSTAIN, never contradict. That test would have caught this and costs nothing on the 109 correct rows.
- 110/110 rows still carry `dedup_key: null`.
- Still distinct from ready[]'s `FIX-CCATO-NTG-ROWS-NOT-PRODUCED-BY-EITHER-SANCTIONED-ENGINE-FORGED-WRITER-ID` (P0, provenance/writer-id). Do not merge them.

WHAT I NOW WITHDRAW:
- 'wrong by construction' / 'structurally wrong' as a characterisation of the gate. Withdrawn. 1/110.
- Priority: I filed it HIGH. On 1-of-110 it is more honestly MEDIUM, which is why this correction carries medium. PO should re-rank.
- 'Auditor agents structurally cannot pass this gate.' NOT DEMONSTRATED and I should not have asserted it. In the exhibit, the probe-mismatch bug alone fully explains the wrong verdict; the auditor-quoting effect is a plausible SECOND mechanism that I did not isolate. It would need an instance where the probe DOES cover the claimed field and an auditor is still wrongly attributed for quoting a claim under audit. No such instance is in the cohort. Treat as a hypothesis to watch, not a finding.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: the other 109 rows are not thereby validated. Whether each claim was actually made by the named agent, and the provenance question, are separate and still open under the P0. This correction is only about my scope claim, not about the cohort's overall soundness.
